alignments.note: כִּי takes whichever connective the ASV wrote for it; here *But*, under rule 14's open list.

Verbless clause whose predicate is the prepositional phrase; the construction-supplied copula and the presentative dummy *there* join the preposition under rules 20 and 49, headed on the preposition. The clause writes no subject but the one nominal סְלִיחָה and the ASV writes no separate English subject, so that nominal is the subject and the phrase the predicate (rule 49's closing paragraph). Unit discontinuous under rule 25.
Suffix takes the pronoun written for it under rule 18.
The ASV writes no *the* for הַסְּלִיחָה; the article is unrepresented under rule 29.
Subject noun keeps its own word.
Purpose preposition takes the complementizer under rule 52; the supplied subject and modal belong to the verb.
Finite passive verb with its subject pronoun, modal and copula under rules 17 and 52, headed on the lexical verb.

review_notes: The competing reading would make *forgiveness* the predicate and give it *there is*, leaving עִם a bare *with*; rule 49's closing paragraph decides for the prepositional predicate, since the clause's only nominal is the English subject of that copula.
